# Story 1.1: Reject over-limit requests with 429 and Retry-After
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API client, I want an over-limit request to be rejected with the time to retry, so that I know when to back off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key with a default limit of N requests per window, when it sends request N+1 within the window, then the response is 429 and carries a Retry-After header giving the seconds until the window resets.
- AC-2: Given an API key that has sent fewer than N requests in the window, when it sends a request, then the request is served and the response is not 429.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Increment a per-key request counter in Redis on each request, expiring with the window (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Apply the default per-key limit from configuration and reject requests over it with 429 (AC: 1)
- [ ] Return Retry-After as the seconds until the counter's window resets (AC: 1)
- [ ] Serve requests under the limit without change (AC: 2)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: Redis is the intended counter store, so counts live in Redis, not in process memory.
- The default limit is the value FR-2 (story 1.2) overrides per key.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-1]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#counter-store]

# Story 1.2: Give an API key a custom limit
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an integration partner, I want my API key to have its own limit, so that my existing burst traffic keeps working unchanged.

# Story 1.3: Keep rate-limit counters across an application restart
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an operator of the public API, I want rate-limit counters to survive a restart, so that restarting the service does not give every client a fresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key that has used part of its limit in the current window, when the application restarts and the key sends more requests, then those requests count against the remaining budget, not a fresh one.
- AC-2: Given an API key at its limit, when the application restarts and the key sends a request, then the response is 429 with a Retry-After header.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Hold per-key counters in Redis, not in process memory, so a restart does not clear them (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Restart the application mid-window and confirm the remaining budget is kept (AC: 1)
- [ ] Restart the application with a key at its limit and confirm the 429 and Retry-After still apply (AC: 1, 2)

## Dev Notes
- CAP-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Redis is the counter store, and counters must not live only in process memory (architecture counter-store).
